Brushing more than twice a day is generally not harmful if done gently and for specific needs, such as removing food debris or after consuming sugary or sticky foods [d1]. Most guidance recommends brushing twice daily for two minutes as the standard for preventing plaque and maintaining oral health [d6,d7]. However, several sources caution that brushing more than three times a day or too vigorously can lead to enamel wear, tooth sensitivity, and gum recession [d3,d4,d5]. Some national associations note that up to three brushings per day may be beneficial in certain cases, such as for people wearing braces [d6]. Therefore, while brushing more than twice daily is acceptable in moderation, excessive frequency or force should be avoided.
